problems.quote: have the roof repaired readily yields The roof was had repaired — a marginal but attested form in formal registers
problems.problem: The passive form 'The roof was had repaired' is not attested in standard English; causative 'have' does not passivize this way.
problems.correction: have the roof repaired does not yield a passive '*The roof was had repaired'; the simple passive 'The roof was repaired' is used instead
problems.verifierReason: Causative 'have' cannot passivize to 'was had repaired'; only simple passive 'was repaired' exists.

problems.quote: the preferred passive is The car was got fixed (with get as a passive auxiliary) or, more commonly, The car was had fixed (formal)
problems.problem: Neither 'The car was got fixed' nor 'The car was had fixed' are standard passive forms; the get-passive is 'The car got fixed' and causative 'have' has no such passive.
problems.correction: the get-passive is 'The car got fixed'; causative 'have' does not form a passive with 'was had fixed'
problems.verifierReason: Get-passive is 'got fixed', not 'was got fixed'; causative 'have' has no 'was had fixed' passive.

problems.quote: When the causative get is passivised, the to-infinitive is retained: The mechanic was got to fix the car (awkward) versus The car got fixed (the get-passive)
problems.problem: 'The mechanic was got to fix the car' is not a grammatical passive of 'get someone to do something'; the construction does not exist.
problems.correction: The passive of 'get someone to do something' is not formed with 'was got to'; instead, 'The mechanic was asked to fix the car' or similar is used
problems.verifierReason: 'Get someone to do' does not passivize to 'was got to do'; alternative passives use 'asked/told'.
